owner_decisions.excerpt:
Prompt: “snow and low temperature outside; warm inside; it will be dark soon.” Criterion: “it is snowing outside” and “the daylight is fading or it is getting dark.”
Prompt: “describe it getting dark as a change.” Criterion: “The fading daylight is expressed as a changing condition with «blir».”
owner_decisions.explanation:
Factual premise: Hidden criteria require current snowfall and current fading daylight, but supplied notes establish only snow outside and darkness coming soon. Snow may already be on the ground; impending darkness need not mean daylight is already fading.
Competing valid answers: Visible directions require describing darkness as a change, but hidden criteria additionally require the particular verb «blir». Other natural change expressions can meet the visible instruction while failing that requirement.
owner_decisions.message:
Factual premise: Hidden criteria require current snowfall and current fading daylight, but supplied notes establish only snow outside and darkness coming soon. Snow may already be on the ground; impending darkness need not mean daylight is already fading.
Competing valid answers: Visible directions require describing darkness as a change, but hidden criteria additionally require the particular verb «blir». Other natural change expressions can meet the visible instruction while failing that requirement.
owner_decisions.quote_english:
Supplied notes describe snow outside and future darkness; criteria require ongoing snowfall and an ongoing change in daylight.
Describe it getting dark as a change; the hidden criterion specifically requires “becomes/is getting.”
owner_decisions.suggested_change:
Specify “it is snowing outside” in the visible note if ongoing snowfall is required. Align the daylight criterion with the note by accepting a change that will happen soon.
Either explicitly request «blir» as supported practice or accept other natural expressions of changing light conditions while evaluating fixed «det» separately.

Snow may already be on the ground; impending darkness need not mean daylight is already fading.", "suggested_change": "Specify “it is snowing outside” in the visible note if ongoing snowfall is required. Align the daylight criterion with the note by accepting a change that will happen soon."}, {"category": "competing_valid_answers", "evidence": "Prompt: “describe it getting dark as a change.” Criterion: “The fading daylight is expressed as a changing condition with «blir».”", "quote_english": "Describe it getting dark as a change; the hidden criterion specifically requires “becomes/is getting.”", "reason": "Visible directions require describing darkness as a change, but hidden criteria additionally require the particular verb «blir». Other natural change expressions can meet the visible instruction while failing that requirement.", "suggested_change": "Either explicitly request «blir» as supported practice or accept other natural expressions of changing light conditions while evaluating fixed «det» separately."}]}
findings.excerpt:
Prompt: “snow and low temperature outside; warm inside; it will be dark soon.” Criterion: “it is snowing outside” and “the daylight is fading or it is getting dark.”
Prompt: “describe it getting dark as a change.” Criterion: “The fading daylight is expressed as a changing condition with «blir».”
findings.explanation:
Factual premise: Hidden criteria require current snowfall and current fading daylight, but supplied notes establish only snow outside and darkness coming soon. Snow may already be on the ground; impending darkness need not mean daylight is already fading.
Competing valid answers: Visible directions require describing darkness as a change, but hidden criteria additionally require the particular verb «blir». Other natural change expressions can meet the visible instruction while failing that requirement.
findings.message:
Factual premise: Hidden criteria require current snowfall and current fading daylight, but supplied notes establish only snow outside and darkness coming soon. Snow may already be on the ground; impending darkness need not mean daylight is already fading.
Competing valid answers: Visible directions require describing darkness as a change, but hidden criteria additionally require the particular verb «blir». Other natural change expressions can meet the visible instruction while failing that requirement.
findings.quote_english:
Supplied notes describe snow outside and future darkness; criteria require ongoing snowfall and an ongoing change in daylight.
Describe it getting dark as a change; the hidden criterion specifically requires “becomes/is getting.”
findings.suggested_change:
Specify “it is snowing outside” in the visible note if ongoing snowfall is required. Align the daylight criterion with the note by accepting a change that will happen soon.
Either explicitly request «blir» as supported practice or accept other natural expressions of changing light conditions while evaluating fixed «det» separately.

findings.suggested_change: Choose one consistent constraint: request two clauses and permit coordination, or retain the two-sentence instruction and align the judge's acceptance guidance with it.

review_runs.summary: Selected source teaches fixed det clearly, uses valid Bokmål, and develops contextual production. Main defects: grammatical alternative rejected in one choice item, two find_fix tasks target omitted words rather than objectively wrong replaceable tokens, and learner-facing level/course commentary. Inspected all 16 exercises. Fourteen serve the objective through fixed-det recognition, construction, agreement, or correction. Two instead test state-versus-change meaning without requiring understanding or use of fixed det.
